title: Adding spatial lookups to RasterField interpolated the user-supplied band index from the lookup tuple straight into the PostGIS SQL template, so a non-integer band index injects SQL.

vulnerable_findings.explanation: The check_raster method injects the lookup.band_lhs and lookup.band_rhs values directly into the SQL fragment via Python string formatting ("%s, %s" % (template_params['lhs'], lookup.band_lhs)). These values originate from the lookup object, which can be influenced by user‑supplied query parameters. Because they are concatenated into the SQL string rather than passed as bound parameters, an attack

findings.explanation: The check_raster method injects the lookup.band_lhs and lookup.band_rhs values directly into the SQL fragment via Python string formatting ("%s, %s" % (template_params['lhs'], lookup.band_lhs)). These values originate from the lookup object, which can be influenced by user‑supplied query parameters. Because they are concatenated into the SQL string rather than passed as bound parameters, an attacker could craft a malicious band index to alter the SQL statement.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass band indices as separate query parameters instead of embedding them via string formatting. For example, use placeholders in the SQL fragment (e.g., "%(lhs)s, %(band_lhs)s") and include the band values in the params list supplied to the database cursor.
